intuition: A rotation moves the last k nodes to the front. Rotating by the full list length changes nothing, so first reduce k by that length. Temporarily connect the tail to the head, then cut the circle just before the nodes that should become the new front.

The last k nodes become a prefix while their relative order stays unchanged. After reducing k modulo length, only one boundary moves: the edge between the original prefix and suffix. Closing the old tail-to-head link temporarily removes the special end of the list. The new tail is then found by position, and cutting after it restores a linear list.
This method rewires existing nodes rather than copying their values into a separate container.

The new tail is the last node of the original prefix of length n-k. Its successor is the first node of the original suffix. Closing the old tail-to-head edge concatenates suffix and prefix; cutting after the new tail preserves every node once in the required order. Two scans locate the old and new tails; existing nodes are reused.

concept.correctness: Closing the tail-to-front link creates a circle containing every original node exactly once. Cutting its predecessor’s link yields exactly the desired suffix followed by the original prefix, with every node present and no cycle left.
